sanskrit: khaḍgaśaktidharair vīrair gadāmusalapāṇibhiḥ prāsatomarahastaiś ca yayau yodhaśatair vṛtaḥ
english: He went out surrounded by hundreds of warriors bearing swords and spears, holding maces and clubs in their hands, and carrying lances and javelins.

sanskrit: siṃhanādaiś ca yodhānāṃ śaṅkhadundubhinisvanaiḥ rathanemisvanaiś cāpi sanāgavarabṛṃhitaiḥ
english: With the lion-roars of the warriors and the sounds of conch-shells and kettledrums, with the rumble of chariot-wheels and the trumpeting of great elephants,

sanskrit: heṣitasvanamiśraiś ca kṣveḍitāsphoṭitasvanaiḥ āsīt kilakilāśabdas tasmin gacchati pārthive
english: Mixed with the neighing of horses and the sounds of war-cries and clapping of arms, a great tumultuous noise arose as the king set forth.

sanskrit: prāsādavaraśṛṅgasthāḥ parayā nṛpaśobhayā dadṛśus taṃ striyas tatra śūram ātmayaśaskaram
english: Women standing on the upper terraces of the finest palace beheld him, the hero who was the maker of his own glory, resplendent with the full majesty of a king.

sanskrit: śakropamam amitraghnaṃ paravāraṇavāraṇam paśyantaḥ strīgaṇās tatra śastrapāṇiṃ sma menire
english: The groups of women gazing upon that slayer of enemies, who was like Indra himself and was a great elephant against the elephants of his foes, bearing weapons in hand, were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa puruṣavyāghro raṇe 'dbhutaparākramaḥ yasya bāhubalaṃ prāpya na bhavanty asuhṛdgaṇāḥ
english: "This is that tiger among men, of wondrous valor in battle — having encountered the might of whose arms, the hosts of enemies survive no more."

sanskrit: iti vāco bruvantyas tāḥ striyaḥ premṇā narādhipam tuṣṭuvuḥ puṣpavṛṣṭīś ca sasṛjus tasya mūrdhani
english: Thus speaking, those women praised the lord of men with great affection and showered a rain of flowers upon his head.

sanskrit: tatra tatra ca viprendraiḥ stūyamānaḥ samantataḥ niryayau parayā prītyā vanaṃ mṛgajighāṃsayā
english: Praised on all sides by foremost brahmins, he departed with great joy into the forest, eager to hunt deer.

sanskrit: sudūram anujagmus taṃ paurajānapadās tadā nyavartanta tataḥ paścād anujñātā nṛpeṇa ha
english: The townspeople and country-folk followed him a great distance, then turned back when they had been dismissed by the king.

sanskrit: suparṇapratimenātha rathena vasudhādhipaḥ mahīm āpūrayām āsa ghoṣeṇa tridivaṃ tathā
english: Then that lord of the earth, with a chariot swift as Garuḍa, filled the earth and the heavens alike with its thunderous noise.

sanskrit: sa gacchan dadṛśe dhīmān nandanapratimaṃ vanam bilvārkakhadirākīrṇaṃ kapitthadhavasaṃkulam
english: As he traveled, that wise one beheld a forest resembling Nandana, strewn with bel, arka, and khadira trees, and crowded with kapittha and dhava trees.

sanskrit: viṣamaṃ parvataprasthair aśmabhiś ca samāvṛtam nirjalaṃ nirmanuṣyaṃ ca bahuyojanam āyatam mṛgasaṃghair vṛtaṃ ghorair anyaiś cāpi vanecaraiḥ
english: It was uneven with mountain slopes and strewn with rocks, waterless and uninhabited by humans, extending for many leagues, filled with terrifying herds of deer and other creatures of the forest.

sanskrit: tad vanaṃ manujavyāghraḥ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ loḍayām āsa duḥṣantaḥ sūdayan vividhān mṛgān
english: That tiger among men, Duḥṣanta, together with his retinue and his army and its mounts, roused that forest and slew various kinds of deer.

sanskrit: bāṇagocarasaṃprāptāṃs tatra vyāghragaṇān bahūn pātayām āsa duḥṣanto nirbibheda ca sāyakaiḥ
english: Duḥṣanta struck down many groups of tigers that came within arrow-range, piercing them through with his shafts.

sanskrit: dūrasthān sāyakaiḥ kāṃś cid abhinat sa nararṣabhaḥ abhyāśam āgatāṃś cānyān khaḍgena nirakṛntata
english: That bull among men split those at a distance with arrows, while others that came near he cut down with his sword.

sanskrit: kāṃś cid eṇān sa nirjaghne śaktyā śaktimatāṃ varaḥ gadāmaṇḍalatattvajñaś cacārāmitavikramaḥ
english: He slew certain black deer with his spear, that foremost of the mighty, skilled in the art of wielding the mace in circles, ranging about with boundless valor.

sanskrit: tomarair asibhiś cāpi gadāmusalakarpaṇaiḥ cacāra sa vinighnan vai vanyāṃs tatra mṛgadvijān
english: He ranged through the forest striking down the wild deer and birds with javelins, swords, maces, clubs, and short swords.

sanskrit: rājñā cādbhutavīryeṇa yodhaiś ca samarapriyaiḥ loḍyamānaṃ mahāraṇyaṃ tatyajuś ca mahāmṛgāḥ
english: The great beasts abandoned the vast forest as it was beaten through by that king of wondrous valor and by his battle-loving warriors.

sanskrit: tatra vidrutasaṃghāni hatayūthapatīni ca mṛgayūthāny athautsukyāc chabdaṃ cakrus tatas tataḥ
english: The herds of deer there, their leaders slain and their groups scattered, cried out here and there in their distress.

sanskrit: śuṣkāṃ cāpi nadīṃ gatvā jalanairāśyakarśitāḥ vyāyāmaklāntahṛdayāḥ patanti sma vicetasaḥ
english: Reaching a dry river, emaciated from the hopelessness of finding water, their hearts exhausted from exertion, they fell senseless to the ground.

sanskrit: kṣutpipāsāparītāś ca śrāntāś ca patitā bhuvi ke cit tatra naravyāghrair abhakṣyanta bubhukṣitaiḥ
english: Overwhelmed by hunger and thirst, weary and fallen to the earth, some among them were devoured there by the hungry tiger-men.

sanskrit: ke cid agnim athotpādya samidhya ca vanecarāḥ bhakṣayanti sma māṃsāni prakuṭya vidhivat tadā
english: Then some forest-dwellers, having kindled fire, properly chopped the flesh and ate it in the prescribed manner.

sanskrit: tatra ke cid gajā mattā balinaḥ śastravikṣatāḥ saṃkocyāgrakarān bhītāḥ pradravanti sma vegitāḥ
english: There some mighty elephants, maddened and wounded by weapons, drew in their trunks in fear and fled with great speed.

sanskrit: śakṛnmūtraṃ sṛjantaś ca kṣarantaḥ śoṇitaṃ bahu vanyā gajavarās tatra mamṛdur manujān bahūn
english: Voiding their dung and urine and streaming much blood, those great wild elephants there trampled many men to death.

sanskrit: tad vanaṃ balameghena śaradhāreṇa saṃvṛtam vyarocan mahiṣākīrṇaṃ rājñā hatamahāmṛgam
english: That forest, thick with buffaloes, with its great animals slain, covered by the king as a cloud of force by its torrents of arrows, shone brilliantly.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato mṛgasahasrāṇi hatvā vipulavāhanaḥ rājā mṛgaprasaṅgena vanam anyad viveśa ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having slain thousands of deer, that king with his great army entered yet another forest in pursuit of game.

sanskrit: eka evottamabalaḥ kṣutpipāsāsamanvitaḥ sa vanasyāntam āsādya mahad īriṇam āsadat
english: Alone now, that one of supreme strength, afflicted by hunger and thirst, reached the end of the forest and came to a vast barren wasteland.

sanskrit: tac cāpy atītya nṛpatir uttamāśramasaṃyutam manaḥprahlādajananaṃ dṛṣṭikāntam atīva ca śītamārutasaṃyuktaṃ jagāmānyan mahad vanam
english: Having crossed even that, the king came to another great forest, endowed with the finest hermitages, delightful to the mind, charming to the eye, and touched by cool breezes.

sanskrit: puṣpitaiḥ pādapaiḥ kīrṇaṃ atīva sukhaśādvalam vipulaṃ madhurārāvair nāditaṃ vihagais tathā
english: Filled with flowering trees, exceedingly pleasant with lush grass, vast, and resonant with the sweet calls of birds —

sanskrit: pravṛddhaviṭapair vṛkṣaiḥ sukhacchāyaiḥ samāvṛtam ṣaṭpadāghūrṇitalataṃ lakṣmyā paramayā yutam
english: Covered by trees with great spreading boughs offering cool shade, its vines swayed by bees, endowed with supreme beauty —

sanskrit: nāpuṣpaḥ pādapaḥ kaś cin nāphalo nāpi kaṇṭakī ṣaṭpadair vāpy anākīrṇas tasmin vai kānane 'bhavat
english: In that forest, not a single tree was without flowers, not one was without fruit, none had thorns, and none was without its covering of bees.

sanskrit: vihagair nāditaṃ puṣpair alaṃkṛtam atīva ca sarvartukusumair vṛkṣaiḥ atīva sukhaśādvalam manoramaṃ maheṣvāso viveśa vanam uttamam
english: Resounding with birds, adorned most beautifully with flowers, with trees bearing blossoms of every season, exceedingly pleasant and delightful — that great archer entered this finest of forests.

sanskrit: mārutāgalitās tatra drumāḥ kusumaśālinaḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ vicitrāṃ sma vyasṛjaṃs te punaḥ punaḥ
english: There, the flower-laden trees loosened by the wind shed again and again a variegated rain of blossoms.

sanskrit: divaspṛśo 'tha saṃghuṣṭāḥ pakṣibhir madhurasvaraiḥ virejuḥ pādapās tatra vicitrakusumāmbarāḥ
english: The trees touching the sky, resounding with birds of sweet voices, shone there in their garments of many-colored flowers.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tatra pravāleṣu puṣpabhārāvanāmiṣu ruvanti rāvaṃ vihagāḥ ṣaṭpadaiḥ sahitā mṛdu
english: On the tender shoots of those trees, bending under the weight of blossoms, the birds cried out softly together with the bees.

sanskrit: tatra pradeśāṃś ca bahūn kusumotkaramaṇḍitān latāgṛhaparikṣiptān manasaḥ prītivardhanān saṃpaśyan sa mahātejā babhūva muditas tadā
english: Beholding many a spot there adorned with heaps of flowers, enclosed by bowers of creepers, filling the heart with joy, that one of great splendor became filled with delight.

sanskrit: parasparāśliṣṭaśākhaiḥ pādapaiḥ kusumācitaiḥ aśobhata vanaṃ tat tair mahendradhvajasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: With trees whose branches intertwined with one another, laden with blossoms, resembling the banner-poles of great Indra, that forest shone magnificently.

sanskrit: sukhaśītaḥ sugandhī ca puṣpareṇuvaho 'nilaḥ parikrāman vane vṛkṣān upaitīva riraṃsayā
english: A breeze, pleasantly cool and fragrant, carrying the pollen of flowers, moved through the forest as if approaching the trees out of a desire to play.

sanskrit: evaṃguṇasamāyuktaṃ dadarśa sa vanaṃ nṛpaḥ nadīkacchodbhavaṃ kāntam ucchritadhvajasaṃnibham
english: The king beheld this forest, endowed with such qualities, beautiful as the Mālini riverbank, resembling a lofty banner.

sanskrit: prekṣamāṇo vanaṃ tat tu suprahṛṣṭavihaṃgamam āśramapravaraṃ ramyaṃ dadarśa ca manoramam
english: And while he was gazing at that forest filled with joyful birds, he also saw a most charming and lovely hermitage.

sanskrit: nānāvṛkṣasamākīrṇaṃ saṃprajvalitapāvakam yatibhir vālakhilyaiś ca vṛtaṃ munigaṇānvitam
english: It was filled with many kinds of trees, its sacred fires blazing brightly, surrounded by ascetics and Vālakhilya sages, attended by troops of holy men.

sanskrit: agnyāgāraiś ca bahubhiḥ puṣpasaṃstarasaṃstṛtam mahākacchair bṛhadbhiś ca vibhrājitam atīva ca
english: With many fire-shrines, its floor spread with flower offerings, and radiant with large, spacious enclosures, it shone brilliantly.

sanskrit: mālinīm abhito rājan nadīṃ puṇyāṃ sukhodakām naikapakṣigaṇākīrṇāṃ tapovanamanoramām tatra vyālamṛgān saumyān paśyan prītim avāpa saḥ
english: O king, on the banks of the holy Mālinī river with its pleasant waters, crowded with many flocks of birds, the hermitage-grove delightful — beholding there the gentle wild creatures, he was filled with joy.

sanskrit: taṃ cāpy atirathaḥ śrīmān āśramaṃ pratyapadyata devalokapratīkāśaṃ sarvataḥ sumanoharam
english: That foremost of chariot-warriors, glorious, arrived at that hermitage, which resembled the world of the gods and was beautiful in every direction.

sanskrit: nadīm āśramasaṃśliṣṭāṃ puṇyatoyāṃ dadarśa saḥ sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ tatra jananīm iva viṣṭhitām
english: He saw the river intertwined with the hermitage, its waters holy, standing there like a mother to all living creatures.

sanskrit: sacakravākapulināṃ puṣpaphenapravāhinīm sakiṃnaragaṇāvāsāṃ vānararkṣaniṣevitām
english: Its sandbars graced with cakravāka birds, flowing with foam and flowers, the home of troops of Kiṃnaras, frequented by monkeys and bears —

sanskrit: puṇyasvādhyāyasaṃghuṣṭāṃ pulinair upaśobhitām mattavāraṇaśārdūlabhujagendraniṣevitām
english: Resounding with holy recitation, beautified by its sandbars, visited by maddened elephants, tigers, and great serpents —

sanskrit: nadīm āśramasaṃbaddhāṃ dṛṣṭvāśramapadaṃ tathā cakārābhipraveśāya matiṃ sa nṛpatis tadā
english: Having seen the river thus joined to the hermitage, and the hermitage itself, that lord of the earth resolved then to enter it.

sanskrit: alaṃkṛtaṃ dvīpavatyā mālinyā ramyatīrayā naranārāyaṇasthānaṃ gaṅgayevopaśobhitam mattabarhiṇasaṃghuṣṭaṃ praviveśa mahad vanam
english: Adorned by the island-graced Mālinī with her lovely banks, the abode of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, beautified like the Gaṅgā, resonant with intoxicated peacocks — he entered that great forest.

sanskrit: tat sa caitrarathaprakhyaṃ samupetya nareśvaraḥ atīva guṇasaṃpannam anirdeśyaṃ ca varcasā maharṣiṃ kāśyapaṃ draṣṭum atha kaṇvaṃ tapodhanam
english: That lord of men, approaching what resembled the garden of Citra-ratha, endowed with manifold excellences and unsurpassed in splendor, then wished to see the great seer Kaṇva, the Kāśyapa, rich in austerities.

sanskrit: rathinīm aśvasaṃbādhāṃ padātigaṇasaṃkulām avasthāpya vanadvāri senām idam uvāca saḥ
english: He stationed his army at the forest gate — chariots, horses crowded together, and masses of infantry — and spoke thus:

sanskrit: muniṃ virajasaṃ draṣṭuṃ gamiṣyāmi tapodhanam kāśyapaṃ sthīyatām atra yāvadāgamanaṃ mama
english: "I shall go to see the pure sage Kāśyapa, that storehouse of austerities. Remain here until I return."

sanskrit: tad vanaṃ nandanaprakhyam āsādya manujeśvaraḥ kṣutpipāse jahau rājā harṣaṃ cāvāpa puṣkalam
english: Having entered that forest resembling Nandana, that lord of men, the king, shed his hunger and thirst and was filled with great rejoicing.

sanskrit: sāmātyo rājaliṅgāni so 'panīya narādhipaḥ purohitasahāyaś ca jagāmāśramam uttamam didṛkṣus tatra tam ṛṣiṃ taporāśim athāvyayam
english: That lord of men, accompanied by his minister and chaplain, having set aside the marks of kingship, went to that excellent hermitage, wishing to see that undying mass of ascetic merit, the sage.

sanskrit: brahmalokapratīkāśam āśramaṃ so 'bhivīkṣya ca ṣaṭpadodgītasaṃghuṣṭaṃ nānādvija gaṇāyutam
english: Beholding that hermitage resembling the world of Brahmā, resounding with the songs of bees, filled with many groups of brahmins,

sanskrit: ṛco bahvṛcamukhyaiś ca preryamāṇāḥ padakramaiḥ śuśrāva manujavyāghro vitateṣv iha karmasu
english: That tiger among men heard the Ṛgvedic hymns being set in motion by foremost Ṛgvedins with their metrical progressions at the various rites being performed there.

sanskrit: yajñavidyāṅgavidbhiś ca kramadbhiś ca kramān api amitātmabhiḥ suniyataiḥ śuśubhe sa tadāśramaḥ
english: The hermitage then shone with those of boundless spirit, well-disciplined, expert in the supplementary sciences of sacrifice, proceeding through their progressions in sequence.

sanskrit: atharvavedapravarāḥ pūgayājñika saṃmatāḥ saṃhitām īrayanti sma padakramayutāṃ tu te
english: Foremost among Atharva-Vedins, honored by assemblies of sacrificers, they chanted the Saṃhitā with its pada and krama recitations.

sanskrit: śabdasaṃskārasaṃyuktaṃ bruvadbhiś cāparair dvijaiḥ nāditaḥ sa babhau śrīmān brahmaloka ivāśramaḥ
english: With other brahmins reciting with proper grammatical refinement, that glorious hermitage rang out, gleaming like the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: yajñasaṃskāravidbhiś ca kramaśikṣā viśāradaiḥ nyāyatattvārthavijñānasaṃpannair vedapāragaiḥ
english: With those expert in sacrificial rites, skilled in sequential recitation training, endowed with the knowledge of logical principles and true meanings, who had crossed to the far shore of the Vedas —

sanskrit: nānāvākyasamāhārasamavāyaviśāradaiḥ viśeṣakāryavidbhiś ca mokṣadharmaparāyaṇaiḥ
english: Skilled in the synthesis and combination of various textual statements, knowledgeable in special rites, devoted to the dharma of liberation —

sanskrit: sthāpanākṣepasiddhāntaparamārthajñatāṃ gataiḥ lokāyatikamukhyaiś ca samantād anunāditam
english: Those who had attained mastery of establishing propositions, refuting objections, and knowing ultimate truths, together with foremost Lokāyata philosophers — with all of these it resounded on every side.

sanskrit: tatra tatra ca viprendrān niyatān saṃśitavratān japahomaparān siddhān dadarśa paravīrahā
english: Here and there he saw foremost brahmins, self-disciplined, firm in their vows, devoted to silent recitation and fire offerings — perfected sages. That destroyer of enemy heroes was filled with wonder.

sanskrit: āsanāni vicitrāṇi puṣpavanti mahīpatiḥ prayatnopahitāni sma dṛṣṭvā vismayam āgamat
english: Beholding the varied seats adorned with flowers, carefully arranged, that lord of the earth was struck with wonder.

sanskrit: devatāyatanānāṃ ca pūjāṃ prekṣya kṛtāṃ dvijaiḥ brahmalokastham ātmānaṃ mene sa nṛpasattamaḥ
english: Seeing the worship of the divine shrines performed by the brahmins, that best of kings imagined himself to be dwelling in the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: sa kāśyapatapoguptam āśramapravaraṃ śubham nātṛpyat prekṣamāṇo vai tapodhanagaṇair yutam
english: He could not satisfy himself gazing at that excellent and auspicious hermitage protected by the austerities of the Kāśyapa, filled with troops of those rich in penance.

sanskrit: sa kāśyapasyāyatanaṃ mahāvratair; vṛtaṃ samantād ṛṣibhis tapodhanaiḥ viveśa sāmātyapurohito 'rihā; viviktam atyarthamanoharaṃ śivam
english: He, the destroyer of enemies, together with his minister and chaplain, entered the abode of the Kāśyapa, surrounded on all sides by sages of great vows and rich in austerities — a solitary, supremely charming, and auspicious place.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato gacchan mahābāhur eko 'mātyān visṛjya tān nāpaśyad āśrame tasmiṃs tam ṛṣiṃ saṃśitavratam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, going forward, that mighty-armed one, having dismissed his ministers, did not see in that hermitage the sage firm in his vows.

sanskrit: so 'paśyamānas tam ṛṣiṃ śūnyaṃ dṛṣṭvā tam āśramam uvāca ka ihety uccair vanaṃ saṃnādayann iva
english: Not finding that sage and seeing the hermitage empty, he called out loudly, "Who is here?" as if making the forest ring with his voice.

sanskrit: śrutvātha tasya taṃ śabdaṃ kanyā śrīr iva rūpiṇī niścakrāmāśramāt tasmāt tāpasīveṣadhāriṇī
english: Then, hearing that sound of his, a maiden came forth from that hermitage, beautiful as Śrī herself, wearing the garb of an ascetic.

sanskrit: sā taṃ dṛṣṭvaiva rājānaṃ duḥṣantam asitekṣaṇā svāgataṃ ta iti kṣipram uvāca pratipūjya ca
english: She, dark-eyed, upon seeing king Duḥṣanta, at once said "Welcome to you" and honored him with due ceremony.

sanskrit: āsanenārcayitvā ca pādyenārghyeṇa caiva hi papracchānāmayaṃ rājan kuśalaṃ ca narādhipam
english: Having honored him with a seat and with water for the feet and the ritual offering, she inquired after the lord of men's health and well-being, O king.

sanskrit: yathāvad arcayitvā sā pṛṣṭvā cānāmayaṃ tadā uvāca smayamāneva kiṃ kāryaṃ kriyatām iti
english: Having honored him duly and inquired about his well-being, she said with a gentle smile: "What may be done for you?"

sanskrit: tām abravīt tato rājā kanyāṃ madhurabhāṣiṇīm dṛṣṭvā sarvānavadyāṅgīṃ yathāvat pratipūjitaḥ
english: Then the king, having been duly honored, spoke to that sweet-spoken maiden with her flawless limbs:

sanskrit: āgato 'haṃ mahābhāgam ṛṣiṃ kaṇvam upāsitum kva gato bhagavān bhadre tan mamācakṣva śobhane
english: "I have come to pay homage to the greatly blessed sage Kaṇva. Where has the venerable one gone, dear lady? Tell me, O lovely one."

sanskrit: śakuntalovāca gataḥ pitā me bhagavān phalāny āhartum āśramāt muhūrtaṃ saṃpratīkṣasva drakṣyasy enam ihāgatam
english: Śakuntalā said: My father the venerable one has gone from the hermitage to gather fruits. Wait a moment — you shall see him return here.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca apaśyamānas tam ṛṣiṃ tayā coktas tathā nṛpaḥ tāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā varārohāṃ śrīmatīṃ cāruhāsinīm
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Not seeing the sage, spoken to thus by her, the king, beholding that woman of noble hips, radiant with beauty, and lovely of smile —

sanskrit: vibhrājamānāṃ vapuṣā tapasā ca damena ca rūpayauvanasaṃpannām ity uvāca mahīpatiḥ
english: Shining with her beauty and with asceticism and self-discipline, endowed with form and youth — thus the lord of the earth spoke:

sanskrit: kāsi kasyāsi suśroṇi kimarthaṃ cāgatā vanam evaṃrūpaguṇopetā kutas tvam asi śobhane
english: "Who are you, O lovely-hipped one? Whose are you? Why have you come to the forest, endowed with such beauty and qualities? Whence are you, O fair one?"

sanskrit: darśanād eva hi śubhe tvayā me 'pahṛtaṃ manaḥ icchāmi tvām ahaṃ jñātuṃ tan mamācakṣva śobhane
english: "By the mere sight of you, O auspicious one, my heart has been stolen away. I wish to know you — tell me, O lovely one."
